question: A head-injured patient opens eyes to pain (E2), makes incomprehensible sounds (V2), and withdraws from pain (M4). What is the GCS score and what airway decision does this mandate?

answers.text: GCS 8 — the airway must be secured with a definitive airway (endotracheal tube)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. E2+V2+M4 = GCS 8. A GCS ≤8 is the threshold at which the patient cannot protect their own airway and requires intubation.
The correct score is E2+V2+M4 = 8, not 10. At GCS ≤8, a definitive airway is required, not merely supplemental oxygen.

answers.text: GCS 8 — no airway intervention is needed unless there is apnoea

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A GCS of 8 is correctly calculated but the management decision is wrong. GCS ≤8 mandates a definitive airway regardless of whether the patient is currently apnoeic.
The GCS calculation is wrong (it is 8 not 6) and needle cricothyrotomy is a last-resort surgical airway, not the first intervention for GCS ≤8.

overallFeedback.feedback: Add each component: Eye (E2) + Verbal (V2) + Motor (M4) = GCS 8. At GCS ≤8 the patient cannot protect their airway — a definitive airway is required.
Well done. GCS 8 (E2V2M4) is the internationally accepted threshold below which the airway cannot be self-protected and intubation is mandatory.
